memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"Then he is to take off these clothes and put on others, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a place that is ceremonially clean."'" - Lev 6:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The priest changes clothes before leaving the sanctuary area. The garments worn at the altar do not go out to the ash heap.

At one level this is simple reverence. What was set apart for God's service stays in God's service. Holy things are not carried casually into ordinary places.

But there is something worth reflecting on here about the rhythm of a life with God. There are garments for the altar and garments for the ash heap, and a wise person knows which they are wearing.

Some Christians never leave the altar — all worship, no work, endlessly seeking experience while ordinary responsibilities go unattended. Others never come to the altar at all, permanently in work clothes, running on empty because they never stop to be with God.

The priest did both. He tended the fire and he carried the ashes. He wore the linen and he changed out of it.

Jesus modelled this rhythm exactly. He went out to a mountainside to pray, and spent the night praying to God (Lk 6:12) — and the next day He was among crowds, healing and teaching. Withdrawal and engagement. Altar and ashes.

Which garment have you been avoiding?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I neglecting time with God, or using it to avoid responsibility?
2. What would a healthier rhythm of worship and work look like this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me the rhythm of coming to You and going out for You. Keep me from neglecting either one. Amen.
